title: Anisotropic noise hypercontractivity
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let $\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For $n\ge 0$, let $T_\rho$ act on functions on $\Omega^n$ by multiplying each product Fourier coefficient at index $a\in\iota^n$ by $\prod_{i:a_i\ne 0}\rho_i$, where $0$ denotes the constant basis index. If $0\le \rho_i\le 1$ for every coordinate, $p\ge 1$, and $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, then $|T_\rho f(x)|^p\le T_\rho(|f|^p)(x)$ for every $x\in\Omega^n$.
hypotheses_covered: probability measure on the sample space
orthonormal real-function basis with a constant-one basis vector
real-valued function on the product space
real exponent p is at least 1
point x in the product space
